chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abi Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt al-Qumi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I, Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Imran, the servant of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), were in his house.

Muhammad ibn Imran said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'We are twelve narrators (or speakers/leaders).' Abu Basir asked him: 'By God, did you hear that from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)?' He made him swear to God once or twice, and he swore that he had heard it. Abu Basir said: 'However, I heard it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abu Basir (a companion of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Who said 'We are twelve narrators' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal records a conversation between companions of the Imams regarding the number of authoritative narrators or leaders. Muhammad ibn Imran reports hearing from Imam al-Sadiq that 'we are twelve,' while Abu Basir clarifies that he heard this specific statement from Imam al-Baqir, highlighting the transmission of this key number within the Ahl al-Bayt lineage. The narration underscores the concept of *Tawatur* (mass transmission) among the companions, as multiple reliable narrators independently confirm the same core doctrine from different Imams, reinforcing the certainty of the Twelve Imams' divinely appointed authority.
